symbols.name: \(d_n\)
symbols.def: A deterministic triangular sequence of category counts indexed by \(n\).

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.def: Law whose observed margin generates each \(O_i\).

symbols.name: \(P^n\)
symbols.def: The \(n\)-fold product of the observed margin of \(P\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal P([-1,1])\)
symbols.def: The set of Borel probability measures on \([-1,1]\).

symbols.name: \(W_1\)
symbols.def: The order-one Wasserstein distance for the Euclidean metric on \([-1,1]\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat G\)
symbols.space: measurable maps from the sample space to \(\mathcal P([-1,1])\)

symbols.name: \(v_x\)
symbols.def: Generic comparison vector in categorical cell \(x\).

symbols.name: \(v\)
symbols.def: Generic nonnegative comparison vector with coordinates \(v_{ay}\).

symbols.name: \(C_\epsilon\)
symbols.def: A finite constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

symbols.name: \(K\)
symbols.def: Degree selected from \(n\), \(d\), and pilot cell geometry by the grouped reconstruction handle.

symbols.name: \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{grp}}\)
symbols.def: Estimator to be derived from the handle in \(\mathrm{def:grouped-reconstruction-handle}\).

symbols.name: \(\rho(n,d)\)
symbols.def: The explicit numerical frontier to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp-all-regime-frontier}\).

standard.name: Uniform treatment overlap for categorical adjustment

assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent with common law equal to the observed margin of \(P\).

definitions.name: Unrestricted categorical causal model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}=\{P: X\in[d], A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\}, P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:fixed\mbox{-}overlap}\}\) for every \(d\ge2\) and fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

definitions.name: Mass-weighted global effect extension
definitions.construction: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\), set \(\bar\mu_a(u)=u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) when \(s(u)>0\) and \(0\) otherwise, set \(\bar\tau(u)=\bar\mu_1(u)-\bar\mu_0(u)\), and set \(F_f(u)=s(u)f(\bar\tau(u))\) for \(f\in\mathcal F_1\).

definitions.name: Total empirical CATE-law estimator
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat q_x\) for every \(x\in[d]\) and output \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{emp}}=\sum_{x=1}^d s(\widehat q_x)\delta_{\bar\tau(\widehat q_x)}\).

definitions.name: All-estimator minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}=\inf_{\widehat G}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^n}[W_1(\widehat G,G_P)^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable \(\mathcal P([-1,1])\)-valued estimators.

definitions.name: Verified lower and upper benchmark scales
Mass-weighted grouped moment-reconstruction handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{grp}}\) by sample splitting, pilot localization of the vectors \(q_x\) into groups indexed jointly by mass shells and effect intervals, unbiased mass-weighted centered Chebyshev effect moments through degree \(K\) using joint four-cell factorial lifts, finite-grid nonnegative Hausdorff-moment programs on the effect intervals, aggregation, exact mass normalization, Rao--Blackwellization, and deterministic fallback; select the grouping, \(K\), grid, and tolerances from \(n\), \(d\), \(\epsilon\), and the exact factorial covariance.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), the causal law \(G_P\) is identified by the observed table as \(G_P=\sum_{x:s(q_x)>0}s(q_x)\delta_{q_{11,x}/s_1(q_x)-q_{01,x}/s_0(q_x)}\), and every table with \(q_x\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) and \(\sum_xs(q_x)=1\) admits a full-data completion in \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\).
statements.justification: This reduction makes lower bounds on observed multinomial tables valid causal lower bounds on the unchanged target.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 identifies only scalar means on the same table, while the present functional retains the entire mass-weighted effect law.
statements.consumer: The reduction lets categorical-profile analyses compute and audit the target directly from observed arm--outcome cells.

statements.statement: For every \(f\in\mathcal F_1\) and \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\), \(|F_f(u)-F_f(v)|\le(4+2/\epsilon)\lVert u-v\rVert_1\). If \(q_x,v_x\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) for \(x\in[d]\) and \(\sum_xs(q_x)=\sum_xs(v_x)=1\), then \(W_1(\sum_xs(q_x)\delta_{\bar\tau(q_x)},\sum_xs(v_x)\delta_{\bar\tau(v_x)})=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_1}|\sum_xF_f(q_x)-\sum_xF_f(v_x)|\).
statements.justification: One simultaneous Lipschitz bound preserves unknown mass weighting and converts Wasserstein recovery into a joint moment problem.
statements.gap: VinayakKongKakade2019Change controls a fixed entity-weighted paired-binomial law; its proof does not contain the mass-weighted ratio extension needed for random observational cells.
statements.consumer: The inequality provides the common deterministic interface for both the empirical estimator and the grouped positive reconstruction.

statements.statement: For all \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the computable estimator \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{emp}}\) is \(\mathcal P([-1,1])\)-valued and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^n}[W_1(\widehat G_{\mathrm{emp}},G_P)^2]\le C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\).
statements.justification: This is a total estimator on the original class and supplies a sharp dense-regime achievability check without trimming null cells.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 bounds scalar plug-in estimators, and VinayakKongKakade2019Change assumes fixed repeated trials; neither gives this probability-valued observational law estimator.
statements.consumer: It gives an immediately implementable conservative law estimate for saturated categorical PONV profiles.

statements.statement: There is \(c_\epsilon>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that, for every \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\), \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge c_\epsilon\min\{d/n,n^{-2/3}\}\), with the lower experiment contained in \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and allowing every measurable probability-valued estimator.
statements.justification: A separated-atom hypercube exposes a full-law difficulty that is invisible to scalar effect averages.
statements.gap: The fuzzy hypotheses in ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 separate a scalar mean, while this construction separates ordered effect laws in \(W_1\) and keeps neighboring observational experiments close.
statements.consumer: The theorem prevents analysts from reporting scalar-optimal error bars as uncertainty for an entire categorical CATE distribution.

statements.statement: For constants depending only on \(\epsilon\), \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\), by a same-class reduction in which \(\int|t|\,dG_P(t)\) equals the normalized \(\ell_1\) separation of two categorical mass vectors.
statements.justification: This floor carries the rare-cell unknown-mass obstruction into the law target without assuming a stand-in CATE functional.
statements.gap: The in-repository scalar theorem supplies the normalized \(\ell_1\) hard family; the new work must prove that its actual causal subexperiment pushes forward to \(G_P\) with the displayed identity.
statements.consumer: It supplies a necessary consistency condition for every probability-valued CATE-law estimator.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\), \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\).
statements.justification: The bracket localizes the unresolved theorem to sparse and transitional categories while preserving every original nuisance feature.
statements.gap: No located paper combines the separated-law and unknown-mass obstructions in one observational risk bracket.
statements.consumer: The bracket gives sample-size diagnostics that remain valid before the exact sparse frontier is solved.

statements.statement: If \(n\ge d^3\), then \(c_\epsilon d/n\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon d/n\) on the full class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\).
statements.justification: This matching regime is the first solved portion of the frontier and a mandatory calibration point for any sparse reconstruction.
statements.gap: Paired-binomial law recovery fixes entity weights and trials, while categorical ATE theory targets a scalar; neither yields the \(d/n\) observational law frontier.
statements.consumer: Analysts with many observations per categorical profile obtain an exact order for full-distribution recovery.

statements.statement: For fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and any sequence \(d_n\ge2\), \(d_n/n\to0\) implies \(R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\to0\), while \(R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\to0\) implies \(d_n/[n\log(ed_n)]\to0\).
statements.justification: The proposition records exactly what the current two-sided theory says about consistency without disguising the logarithmic gap.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 gives scalar consistency restrictions, not necessary and sufficient regions for a probability law under \(W_1\).
statements.consumer: Study designers can distinguish a proved safe regime from a proved impossible regime for categorical heterogeneity reporting.

statements.statement: For fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and any sequence \(d_n\ge2\), \(\sup_{n\ge1}nR_{n,d_n,\epsilon}<\infty\) if and only if \(\sup_{n\ge1}d_n<\infty\).
statements.justification: This exact boundary is available even though the sparse minimax rate is not yet known.
statements.gap: Existing population-of-parameters rates index fixed entities and trials; they do not characterize root-risk behavior under growing observational categories.
statements.consumer: The result tells practitioners when ordinary parametric precision for the whole CATE law is mathematically impossible.

statements.statement: Determine an explicit numerical function \(\rho(n,d)\), not defined by a minimax optimization, and derive choices inside \(\mathrm{def:grouped-reconstruction-handle}\) such that \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le\rho(n,d)\le C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\) and \(c_\epsilon\rho(n,d)\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^n}[W_1(\widehat G_{\mathrm{grp}},G_P)^2]\le C_\epsilon\rho(n,d)\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\); the derivation must yield the exact consistency region, reproduce the \(d/n\) lower bound on the separated-atom hypercube, and give a nonconstant guarantee for two effect clusters with unknown unequal masses and propensities at both overlap boundaries.
statements.justification: The open object is the full sparse-to-dense frontier, including one coherent positive estimator and a same-class all-estimator converse.
statements.gap: VinayakKongKakade2019Change fixes equal trials and entity weights, LeeBacakKennedy2025 assumes smooth mixing densities with observed trial counts, and HanJiaoWeissman2018 has one-population local moments; none controls the coupled mass-weighted treated--control moment process here.
statements.consumer: A solved frontier would calibrate CATE-distribution reporting for dexamethasone response profiles without claiming individual treatment effects or exact nonresponder atoms.

sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling under identified treatment effects.
sampling_model.overlap: Known fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), imposed only on occupied cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The masses \(p_x\), propensities \(e_x\), and outcome regressions \(\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\) are all unknown; null cells, effect ties, and boundary outcome means are retained.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{emp}}=\sum_{x=1}^ds(\widehat q_x)\delta_{\bar\tau(\widehat q_x)},\qquad c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives the lower bound \(R^*(d,n)\gtrsim[d/(n\log n)]^2+1/n\) for a scalar regression mean when \(d\lesssim n\log n\).
Theorems 2.1--2.2 give matching sparse-regime \(W_1\) rates for a change law from independent parameter pairs observed through a common fixed number of binomial trials per arm.
Theorem 1 gives a near-sharp sorted \(\ell_1\) risk for an unlabeled discrete distribution using local moment matching and positive-measure reconstruction.
Corollary 2 bounds pointwise bias and variance for a smooth density-difference estimator with observed heterogeneous trial counts.

tldr: High-dimensional categorical adjustment creates two coupled difficulties for recovering treatment-effect heterogeneity: each effect location is a ratio of two noisy arm means, and the same unknown cell mass determines both its sampling intensity and its weight in the target law. The theorem program identifies the law from the observed four-cell table, gives a total empirical probability-valued estimator, proves the all-regime bracket \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\), and closes the dense regime at order \(d/n\) when \(n\ge d^3\). Its first-class open kernel is the exact sparse-to-dense scale: a mass-weighted joint factorial-moment reconstruction must be tuned and matched by a same-class converse without smoothness, mass floors, effect separation, tie exclusions, trimming, or known nuisances.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal theory treats scalar averages, while population-of-parameters theory fixes entity weights or trial counts. Neither literature determines the squared \(W_1\) risk of the population-weighted categorical CATE law when masses, propensities, and both arm regressions are unknown.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied regime is a coupled multinomial-ratio inverse problem in which null cells and tied effects are legal and a valid output must be one coherent probability measure.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies observed-law identification, a mass-weighted Lipschitz extension, a computable empirical estimator, two complementary lower constructions, the exact dense and parametric-risk boundaries, and a concrete positive grouped-moment handle for resolving the remaining frontier.

related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 provides the closest observational setup and motivates the sparse-to-dense organization, but its target is a scalar ATE or regression mean. VinayakKongKakade2019Change is the closest law-valued analogue: it estimates the distribution of differences between paired Bernoulli parameters using fixed common trials and equal entity weighting. VinayakKongValiantKakade2019 and TianKongValiant2017 establish that coherent mixing-law estimators can outperform empirical plug-in rules in sparse fixed-trial experiments. HanJiaoWeissman2018 supplies the local moment-feasibility architecture adapted here, but its primitive is one multinomial probability per label rather than a mass-weighted treated--control ratio. LeeBacakKennedy2025 studies observed heterogeneous trial counts under smooth mixing densities; its conditional fixed-trial experiment does not include endogenous unknown target weights or unrestricted atomic effect laws. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 concerns smooth CATE-function loss rather than the pushforward population law. ChernozhukovFernandezValLuo2018 motivates full effect-distribution reporting, but its regular sorting inference does not cover this sparse unrestricted atomic model. MizuguchiSawamura2023 supplies the applied consumer: a fitted dexamethasone CATE histogram is interpreted as response heterogeneity even though the true cell effects are unavailable.
technical_internal_limitation: The brackets do not determine the exact transitional rate. A scalar localized polynomial bound cannot be promoted by interchanging expectation and the supremum over Lipschitz tests. The grouped certificate must be checked with exact factorial covariances on the separated-atom hypercube and on two clusters with unequal unknown weights and boundary propensities. Failure on either test invalidates the grouped route, while a genuine exact-class collision theorem would require a pivot.
honest_scope: The target is the population law of conditional mean effects, not the distribution of individual potential-outcome differences. Wasserstein recovery alone does not validate a claim that \(G_P\) has an atom at zero. The dense frontier, the two-sided global bracket, and the parametric-risk boundary are stated as theorem targets; the exact sparse/transitional rate and exact consistency region remain explicit open content. As a sanity reduction, fixed \(d\) and \(n\to\infty\) give \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}\asymp_\epsilon n^{-1}\), while \(n\ge d^3\) gives \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}\asymp_\epsilon d/n\).

seed_details.one_line: Sharp all-regime squared \(W_1\) recovery of the population-weighted categorical CATE law under unknown masses, propensities, and arm regressions.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the exact sparse-to-dense minimax frontier for the original population CATE law.
seed_details.anchor_locations_read: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Introduction, Theorem 2, its fuzzy-hypothesis construction in Appendix C, and Section 8; VinayakKongKakade2019Change, Sections 1.1 and 2, Theorems 2.1--2.2, and the Bernstein-polynomial proof around equations (20)--(22); LeeBacakKennedy2025, Introduction, Corollary 2, Appendix A, and Section 6.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar localized polynomial certificate by simultaneous mass-weighted treated--control factorial moments followed by positive-measure reconstruction and uniform Lipschitz-test control.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for categorical CATE law Wasserstein minimax, mass-weighted paired binomial change distribution, and observational population-of-parameters recovery found no theorem with unknown multinomial weights and propensities.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from VinayakKongKakade2019Change after conditioning on each cell count and pushing the joint mixing law through subtraction.
seed_details.rebuttal: Conditioning fixes counts that are generated by the same unknown masses weighting the target, deletes unseen mass, and leaves arm counts coupled through unknown propensities; the separated-atom \(d/n\) floor also contradicts a scalar-rate transplantation.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace regular Hadamard sorting and pointwise fixed-mixture test inversion by a simultaneous positive-measure feasibility set for random observational cell intensities.

literature_map: The chosen kernel is anchored to ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, whose Introduction and Section 8 organize unrestricted categorical confounding around sparse-to-dense phase changes and whose Theorem 2 uses fuzzy hypotheses for a scalar regression mean. VinayakKongKakade2019Change, Theorems 2.1--2.2, estimates a law of paired Bernoulli-parameter changes by fitting the bivariate mixing law and pushing it through subtraction; equation (21) shows the polynomial approximation step that must be altered. VinayakKongValiantKakade2019 proves sparse fixed-trial NPMLE optimality for a one-parameter population, and TianKongValiant2017 supplies the earlier homogeneous-trial earth-mover benchmark. HanJiaoWeissman2018, especially Section 2 and Theorem 1, localizes empirical count scales, matches factorial moments in a positive feasibility program, and controls all Lipschitz tests; the present handle adapts that construction to four coordinates and unknown mass weights. LeeBacakKennedy2025 conditions on heterogeneous observed trials and imposes smooth mixing densities, so Corollary 2 does not subsume unrestricted random observational cells. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 studies smooth CATE-function estimation and supplies causal higher-order lower-bound techniques, but not law-valued loss. Searches over these papers' references and current destination-keyword pairs found no closer result covering the conjunction of unknown masses, unknown propensities, two noisy outcome regressions, arbitrary null cells and ties, and uniform all-regime squared \(W_1\) risk.

novelty_justification.repo_axis: The accepted optimal-value run estimates one scalar nonsmooth functional under the same unknown masses and propensities; its lower priors and Jackson certificate neither output a probability law nor control the supremum over Lipschitz tests. The accepted proxy effect-law run gives collision-stable positive reconstruction only for a fixed latent dimension under spectral proxy conditions. The present kernel retains the original unrestricted observed-law class and requires a growing-category mass-weighted joint reconstruction plus a same-class converse.
novelty_justification.published_axis: VinayakKongKakade2019Change is the closest law target, but its entities have equal target weight and a common fixed number of trials in each arm. ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 is the closest causal experiment, but its target is scalar. LeeBacakKennedy2025 adds heterogeneous fixed trial counts only under smooth densities. The proposed dense \(d/n\) lower bound and the unknown sparse frontier arise from the interaction of observational occupancy, arm splitting, ratio effects, and target weighting, which none of these comparators contains.
novelty_justification.strict_delta: The theorem-level delta is not pairing, grouping, or positive reconstruction by itself. It is a uniform risk theory for one computable probability-valued estimator and every competing estimator on the original unknown-mass observational experiment, with the separated-atom dense frontier and the rare-mass scalar floor as simultaneous mandatory reductions.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic:
Sharp all-regime recovery of the population CATE law with unrestricted high-dimensional discrete confounders. Observe n iid (X,A,Y), X in [d], binary A and Y, under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and known fixed overlap epsilon in (0,1/2). Cell masses are arbitrary and unknown; propensities and both outcome regressions are unknown, with no smoothness, positive mass floor, effect separation, or exclusion of ties. The target G_P=sum_{x:p_x>0} p_x delta_(mu_1x-mu_0x) is the population law of conditional mean effects. Determine, up to epsilon-only constants and uniformly over n>=1,d>=2, inf_Ghat sup_P E[W1(Ghat,G_P)^2]. Construct one explicit computable probability-valued estimator and a matching all-estimator converse, deriving consistency and parametric-risk boundaries; leave the exact rate open. The full sparse-to-dense frontier is the kernel: a dense-regime theorem alone, a scalar-functional collection, or a one-sided bound is insufficient. Novelty must survive Vinayak-Kong-Kakade paired-binomial change-law estimation and Lee-Bacak-Kennedy fixed heterogeneous trial counts by handling unknown mass-weighted observational sampling. Consumer: categorical-profile CATE-distribution analyses motivated by Mizuguchi-Sawamura's dexamethasone/PONV study. This does not identify individual potential-outcome differences or validate zero-atom claims from W1 alone. Delegate estimator algebra and tuning, retaining the original law class. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A separated-atom hypercube keeps the observed experiments close while moving the CATE law in Wasserstein distance. Together with a total cellwise plug-in construction, the presolve reports a matching risk of order d/n when n is at least d cubed, on the original unrestricted model. An independently checked eight-cell instance has positive probabilities, exact neighboring transport cost 1/512, and n-sample KL approximately 0.063. This shows why the scalar optimal-value rate cannot simply be transplanted. A mass-weighted Lipschitz extension and a deterministic positive grouped moment-reconstruction certificate provide a route beyond this regime. Paired-binomial law recovery and fixed heterogeneous trial-count estimation are existing precedents; grouping alone is not novelty. These derivations and comparisons require independent verification.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Control and optimize the joint moment-estimation process uniformly over all Lipschitz test functions under arbitrary unknown cell masses and propensities, and prove a matching converse in the remaining sample-size/category regimes. The dense result alone does not complete the promised paper.
EARLY KILL TEST: Test the proposed joint reconstruction certificate, with exact factorial covariances, on the explicit separated-atom hypercube and on two effect clusters with unknown unequal masses and propensities at both overlap boundaries. It must respect the d/n dense lower bound and deliver a concrete nontrivial clustered bound without known-weight assumptions or discarded null cells; a contradictory scalar-rate certificate must be abandoned, and an affirmative exact-class generic collision or obstruction should stop or pivot the run.

literature_checklist.author: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 2 gives a scalar high-dimensional categorical causal lower bound using fuzzy hypotheses, while Section 8 leaves tighter constructive rates open.

literature_checklist.author: Vinayak, Kong, and Kakade
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 2.1--2.2 recover a paired-binomial change law under equal entity weights and common fixed trials per arm.

literature_checklist.author: Han, Jiao, and Weissman
literature_checklist.one_line: Section 2 and Theorem 1 develop local factorial-moment matching with positive-measure reconstruction under Wasserstein loss.

literature_checklist.author: Lee, Baćak, and Kennedy
literature_checklist.one_line: Corollary 2 treats smooth density differences with observed heterogeneous trial counts, not unknown target weights or unrestricted atoms.

literature_checklist.author: Vinayak, Kong, Valiant, and Kakade
literature_checklist.one_line: The population NPMLE is minimax for sparse homogeneous-trial binomial mixtures and provides a coherent-law estimator precedent.

literature_checklist.author: Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, and Luo
literature_checklist.one_line: The sorted-effects theorems give simultaneous inference under regular sorting, motivating but not covering arbitrary sparse atomic ties.

literature_checklist.author: Mizuguchi and Sawamura
literature_checklist.one_line: The dexamethasone study uses fitted CATE distributions to discuss heterogeneous response while acknowledging that true conditional effects are unavailable.

literature_checklist.author: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper derives minimax rates for smooth heterogeneous-effect functions and supplies higher-order causal lower-bound techniques.
